cards.title: NPCs that actually live
cards.pitch: Per-NPC memory, planning, and social dynamics pushed far enough that the simulation reads as alive. TTS/STT for first-person immersion instead of typed dialogue. The work already done in LifeSim's 4-layer AI and Kokoro/Moonshine speech stack is the foundation — the research is how far it stretches before cost or coherence breaks.
cards.the_question: What's the right split between symbolic planning and LLM inference per NPC-tick to keep a village coherent for 20+ hours of play at under $1/hr? Where does emergent behaviour stop looking like reasoning and start looking like noise?
needs: Cheap reliable local inference (8-13B) for the Layer-2 NPC-decision tier
Grammar-constrained decoding so JSON actions never break the sim
Long-horizon memory compression that survives 20+ in-game days

cards.title: LLM structured-output reliability
cards.pitch: The hardest part of shipping agentic systems isn't the reasoning — it's the JSON not breaking. Grammar-constrained decoding, self-repair loops, schema-shape validators, and evaluation harnesses that measure format-accuracy as a first-class metric alongside task-accuracy.
cards.the_question: What's the minimum-overhead enforcement stack — across Anthropic tool-use, Ollama grammars, and homegrown validators — that gives multi-agent systems contract-level reliability on their internal JSON?
needs: An open eval harness that tracks format regression across model versions
Generalised self-repair (parse-fail → regenerate with error context → validate) as a library
Benchmark corpus of the 20 most common schema breakages

cards.title: Multi-agent orchestration
cards.pitch: Team-of-agents patterns that run for hours, spend within a budget, route messages through a typed bus, and leave an audit trail you can reconstruct a decision from. AITrading's team_orchestrator + MCP architecture is the existing implementation; the research is what else this pattern is good for — autonomous code review, research operators, long-horizon simulation steering.
cards.the_question: How do you run an agent-of-agents system overnight without it drifting, looping, or silently burning budget? What's the minimum-viable supervision loop?
needs: An ergonomic MCP-server pattern for inter-agent routing
Budget-accounting instrumentation that surfaces as first-class data, not logs
Ephemeral-agent lifecycle (spawn / task / reduce / dispose) as a library

cards.title: Procedural world generation
cards.pitch: Infinite worlds with continuous streaming, WFC and marching-cubes backends working together, biome systems that respect global constraints while producing local variety. Remain's terrain + scatter + forest and LifeSim's AI-first world gen both push in this direction; the unified next step is a framework that lets either share the underlying solver.
cards.the_question: What's the right seam between solvers (WFC / noise / marching cubes / L-system) and game logic so the same world-gen stack powers a survival sandbox and a multiplayer grassland?
needs: A shared streaming-chunk API across Unity, WebGPU, and Hytale SDK back-ends
Constraint-propagation primitives faster than current per-cell WFC
Biome-transition blending that survives player fast-travel

cards.title: Real-time graphics R&D
cards.pitch: Cloud volumetrics, GPU grass + scatter, 7-pass retro post-processing, Gaussian-splatting experiments. This lives at /tech-art/ as a showcase, but the research thread continues — the next waves are compute-driven fluids with proper boundary conditions, Gaussian splats as a game-asset format, temporal super-resolution without the TAA ghosting.
cards.the_question: Can a solo developer ship a WebGPU game with Gaussian-splat assets, reconstructed per-frame at 60 FPS, on consumer hardware?
needs: A faster splat-renderer than the current best-public implementation
A pipeline that takes photogrammetry → splats → compressed runtime format
WebGPU subgroup/quad operations (when they ship) for compute-side splat sort

cards.title: Algorithmic trading research
cards.pitch: Beyond AITrading-as-is: better signals (options-flow, cross-market regime detection, LLM-extracted alpha), principled Kelly sizing, walk-forward-with-regime-split validation, conformal prediction thresholds calibrated per ticker. The framework exists; the open problem is surfacing non-obvious alpha from unstructured sources.
cards.the_question: What's the honest Sharpe ceiling for a solo retail quant with 1 GPU, Ollama, and a year's worth of experimentation budget?
needs: Cleaner options-chain + unusual-activity data
Evaluation harness that separates data-mining overfit from genuine alpha
Cross-asset regime features that don't require hand-labelling

cards.title: Training on massive setups
cards.pitch: Multi-GPU distributed training, pipeline parallelism, efficient fine-tuning, long-context pre-training on synthetic data. Not currently possible on a single RTX 3070; the ambition is explicit. Where the capacity goes: bespoke NPC-brain models for LifeSim, specialised vision models for technical-art tasks, domain-tuned trading models.
cards.the_question: What's the per-GPU-hour floor for training a useful 3B-parameter task model from scratch in 2026?
needs: Compute (cloud or co-op)
A well-scoped problem that justifies training-from-scratch vs fine-tuning an open model
Distributed-training expertise (DeepSpeed / FSDP / Megatron patterns)

cards.title: GPU compute for simulation
cards.pitch: Particle systems, rigid and soft-body physics, fluid solvers — running as compute shaders instead of engine physics. The Qatar 360° project has a 2D incompressible fluid sim; Remain has a 256×256 Navier-Stokes cloud layer. The next step is 3D compute fluid running at game tick rates, and compute-driven rigid body with constraint solving.
cards.the_question: Where's the WebGPU-vs-CUDA performance gap for particle/physics sims in 2026, and can WebGPU close enough of it to ship AAA-grade simulation in a browser game?
needs: WGSL atomic + subgroup operations matching Vulkan feature parity
A reference 3D fluid solver for WebGPU (currently nothing public at quality)
Benchmarking corpus (WebGPU vs CUDA vs Metal) for real game workloads

cards.title: Energy & ecology engineering
cards.pitch: Thermal modelling of building envelopes, renewable-energy sizing, efficiency optimisation for residential and agricultural installations. Background from prior work on heat isolation, renewables, and the [solar-install modelling](gaec_solar) for a French dairy farm. Applying software craft — simulation, optimisation, tooling — to decarbonisation is the direction.
cards.the_question: What's missing between the existing off-the-shelf thermal-simulation tools (EnergyPlus, IES-VE) and what a small-farm / retrofit client actually needs? Where does better tooling cut material misuse?
needs: Partnership with a renewable-energy or thermal-retrofit firm for real workloads
Access to a dataset of actual energy-bill outcomes for calibration
A user cohort for whom current tooling is too heavyweight
